name: Limburg Standard Dutch (Netherlands)

ancestors.notes: Standard Dutch of the Netherlands; the Limburg regional standard differs from it in the realisation of /ɣ/ and /x/.

location.notes: the province of Limburg in the Netherlands, a region-level point. The teacher-corpus towns are Sittard, Geleen and Roermond. [Wikidata Q1093 P625]

notes: Regionally coloured Standard Dutch of Dutch Limburg: the standard language as spoken by educated speakers from the province, not the Limburgish dialects (li). The data are the teacher corpus of Van Hout et al. (1999), region N-Z (Zuid), with the towns Geleen, Roermond and Sittard (van der Harst & Van de Velde 2007, p. 178; van der Harst 2011, p. 55). van der Harst (2011, p. 53): the teachers 'are professional language users who are assumed to speak the standard language on a daily basis'. The spec is a delta over nl-NL: it inherits every grapheme, positional entry, word exception, allophone rule and the stress block, and it states only the features below. MODELLED (1) /ɣ/ AS THE VOICELESS VELAR [x], the 'soft g'. van der Harst & Van de Velde (2007, p. 184): 'In Nederlands Limburg (N-Z) vinden we zoals verwacht vooral velairen (52.5%) en palato-velairen (42.5%). De uvulair komt er maar zelden voor (5%) in dit type taalgebruik.' Table 4 (p. 184) gives the voicing for N-Z: -stem 77.5%, +-stem 5.0%, +stem 17.5%. p. 185: 'In Nederlands-Limburg (N-Z) wordt bijna nooit geschraapt'. p. 189 states the regional norm: 'in de regio's onder de rivieren (N-Z en de vier Vlaamse regio's) is de stemloze velair de norm'; Table 6 (pp. 189-190) has ve1, the voiceless unscraped velar, as the most frequent N-Z variant (16 of 40 tokens). p. 192: 'Limburg onttrekt zich echter volledig aan dit patroon en heeft een eigen uitspraaknorm. Daar komen vooral stemloze velairen en palato-velairen voor. Nederlands-Limburg deelt die uitspraaknorm voor /γ/ met Vlaanderen.' The measured context is a word-initial stressed /ɣ/ after a schwa and before /œy/, in the carrier sentence 'in de guize horen we g' (pp. 178-179). The positional entry for ⟨g⟩ states [x] in every position. The word-final [x] is the velar place of /ɣ/ with the final devoicing of nl-NL; the source does not measure the coda. The child states both values itself, so it keeps the velar place whatever dorsal value nl-NL gives ⟨g⟩. The nl-NL grapheme ⟨berg⟩ spells the same ⟨g⟩ inside one key, so the spec restates it as [bɛrx] in both positions: bergen [ˈbɛrxən], and berggebied degeminates to [ˈbɛrxəbit] as in nl-NL. The copy keeps the [r] of the nl-NL entry, so a change to that entry in nl-NL must be copied here. The inherited rules act on the new [x]: NL_CODA_DEVOICE_* devoices a coda obstruent before it (zandgrond [ˈzɑntxrɔnt]), and collapse_geminates merges it with a preceding [x], so ⟨g⟩ next to ⟨ch⟩ gives one [x] (lachgas [ˈlɑxɑs], Egchel [ˈɛxəl]). The nl-NL grapheme ⟨veld⟩ is one slot, so its [d] does not devoice before the new [x] (veldgrijs [ˈvɛldxrɛis]); that is an nl-NL limit. (2) WORD-INITIAL ⟨v⟩ AS VOICED [v]. Van de Velde (2016, p. 10), for the same teacher regions: 'In de Randstad gebruikt 41% die v aan het begin van een woord, in de middenregio 53% en in het zuiden 65%.' The positional entry for ⟨v⟩ states the default [v] and the word-final [f] itself, so a devoiced initial ⟨v⟩ in the positional map of nl-NL does not reach this spec. If nl-NL devoices initial ⟨v⟩ with an allophone rule instead, this spec must switch that rule off by its id. (3) ⟨ch⟩ AS THE VOICELESS VELAR [x]. No opened source measures /x/ in Dutch Limburg; the source above measures /ɣ/ only. The value rests on the regional norm it names: 'Limburg onttrekt zich echter volledig aan dit patroon en heeft een eigen uitspraaknorm. Daar komen vooral stemloze velairen en palato-velairen voor. Nederlands-Limburg deelt die uitspraaknorm voor /γ/ met Vlaanderen' (van der Harst & Van de Velde 2007, p. 192). In the Flemish standard that Limburg shares this norm with, ⟨ch⟩ is the voiceless velar: Verhoeven (2005, p. 244): 'Belgian Dutch has a voiced and voiceless velar fricative: these are absent in the Netherlands. The Netherlands has a voiceless uvular fricative which does not occur in Belgian Dutch', with x for ⟨ch⟩ in chijl in the word list. The Maastricht dialect has the same velar pair and no uvular fricative (Gussenhoven & Aarts 1999, pp. 155-156, x in the word for 'laugh'); that is dialect data, cited as background only. So the spec gives ⟨ch⟩ the same voiceless velar [x] as ⟨g⟩, and the voiceless onset /ɣ/ of the norm and /x/ meet in one value: lachen [ˈlaːxən], acht [ˈɑxt]. The nl-NL keys that spell the same ⟨ch⟩ inside one slot are restated with [x]: ⟨sch⟩ as [sx] (school [ˈsxoːl]) with the word-final [s] of nl-NL (logisch [ˈloːxis]), and ⟨brecht⟩ as [brɛxt]. The nl-NL word exception tjerkgaast is restated as [ˈtʃɛrkxaːst], because a word exception bypasses the grapheme layer. Every copy keeps the other segments of the nl-NL entry, so a change to that entry in nl-NL must be copied here. NOT MODELLED: (a) The palato-velar realisation of /ɣ/ (42.5%, p. 184). The paper scores it as a category and gives no conditioning context, so no rule selects it. (b) /r/. Van Bezooijen & van den Berg (2004, p. 94) describe South Limburg as 'een gebied met vrijwel uitsluitend huig-r. De Gooise r komt hier nauwelijks of niet voor, evenmin als de tongpunt-r.' This is a background statement about the home region of a listener group, with no measurement, so the spec takes the nl-NL value of ⟨r⟩. (c) The long mid vowels and the diphthongs. Voeten (2021, p. 166): /eː/ is a vowel 'which the three non-Randstad regions in the Netherlands also diphthongize less strongly than the Randstad region', and 'For the vowels /øː,oː,œy/, Netherlands-Limburg goes along with the Flemish regions, in having higher F1s.' p. 171: 'The between-region effects are phonetically gradual: there are no regions which categorically do not diphthongize their vowels'. These are gradient differences with no category change, so the spec takes the nl-NL vowel values. van der Harst (2011, p. 200) adds that 'N-S differs more from the other Dutch regions than it does from the Flemish regions' in the vowels. (d) Tone and pitch accent belong to the Limburgish dialects; no opened source measures them in regional Standard Dutch.

sources.author: van der Harst, S. & Van de Velde, H.
sources.title: 17 g's in het Standaardnederlands?
sources.notes: Auditory transcription of word-initial /ɣ/ by 160 teachers of Dutch in eight regions. Tables 3 and 4 give place and voicing per region; the N-Z (Dutch Limburg) norm is the voiceless velar.

sources.author: Verhoeven, J.
sources.title: Belgian Standard Dutch
sources.publisher: Journal of the International Phonetic Association 35(2), 243-247
sources.notes: Belgian Dutch has a voiced and a voiceless velar fricative, and no uvular; the word list gives x for ⟨ch⟩ in chijl. Cited for ⟨ch⟩, with the shared Limburg-Flemish /ɣ/ norm of van der Harst & Van de Velde (2007, p. 192).

sources.author: Gussenhoven, C. & Aarts, F.
sources.title: The dialect of Maastricht
sources.publisher: Journal of the International Phonetic Association 29(2), 155-166
sources.notes: Dialect data: the consonant chart has the velar fricatives x and ɣ and no uvular fricative; ⟨ch⟩ is x in the word for 'laugh'. Background for ⟨ch⟩ only; the dialect is not the regional standard.

sources.author: Van de Velde, H.
sources.title: Hetzelfde, maar toch anders. Regionale variatie binnen het Standaardnederlands
sources.notes: Rates of voiced word-initial v in the teacher corpus: Randstad 41%, middle 53%, south 65%, north 9%. Only the first page of the article was read.

sources.author: van der Harst, S.
sources.title: The Vowel Space Paradox: A Sociophonetic Study on Dutch
sources.notes: The teacher corpus: the speakers, the region labels and the towns; N-S is the most distinct Netherlandic region in the vowels.

sources.author: Voeten, C. C.
sources.title: Regional variation in ongoing sound change: The case of the Dutch diphthongs
sources.notes: Gradient regional differences in the diphthongisation and lowering of the long mid vowels and diphthongs; cited for the vowel features the spec does not model.

sources.author: Van Bezooijen, R. & van den Berg, R.
sources.title: De Gooise r: wie ziet er wat in en waarom?
sources.notes: Background statement on the uvular r of South Limburg; cited for the /r/ feature the spec does not model.
